source_review.notes: Checked all ten structured references. WCAG 2.2 is the current W3C Recommendation dated December 12, 2024 and supports complete-process, keyboard, focus, status, input, authentication, and conformance claims while explicitly not covering every user need. Current WAI APG supports pattern and keyboard guidance without being treated as automatic conformance. Current OWASP ASVS and session/CSRF guidance support the browser security controls with architecture-specific limitations. Current Backstage architecture and catalog documentation support composed shell/plugin/entity concepts and source-controlled metadata ownership. DORA's January 12, 2026 guidance supports journey, feedback, independence, and balanced-measurement claims. ISO 9241-210:2019 remains current after 2025 confirmation. GOV.UK guidance supports end-to-end, front-to-back, cross-channel, inclusive, safe, and recoverable service design.

evidence: Checked P=(J,C,S,O,E,A,G), evidence times t_s, t_o, t_p, age a(e), plugin set Q, universal quantifier, membership, and subset notation against first use and Definitions and Notation.
Checked tuple, function, set, subscript, and logical syntax with the repository GitHub-math validator.
notation_and_syntax.notes: All symbols are defined and the portal presentation state S remains distinct from source time t_s.

evidence: Executed portal-operation-projection under Python 3.14.4 and reproduced seven operations, three terminal states, four actionable records, two stale records, and zero unsafe successes.
Recomputed terminal states as one succeeded plus two failed; actionable states as one needs_action plus two failed plus one unknown; stale ages as 75 and 120.
The executable check detected and corrected the initial expected actionable count of three to four before completion.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The projection is synthetic and its 60-unit stale threshold is illustrative, not a universal service objective.

evidence: Expanded the seven-element portal tuple against journey, resource, presentation, operation, evidence, authorization, and guardrail prose.
Derived evidence age a(e)=t_p-t_s only when source time, provenance, and clock assumptions hold.
Checked that local plugin properties for each q in Q do not entail composed end-to-end accessibility or availability.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The formulas define projections and non-compositionality cautions rather than proving a portal implementation correct.

evidence: Reviewed loading, empty, stale, partial, denied, not-found, invalid, submitting, accepted, running, needs-action, succeeded, failed, cancelled, timed-out, and unknown states.
Checked refresh, back/forward, deep link, concurrent tabs, duplicate submission, response loss, plan drift, session expiry, provider outage, and portal outage.
Checked keyboard, screen reader, zoom, reflow, high contrast, reduced motion, voice, touch, focus obstruction, status announcement, and accessible authentication.
Checked CSRF, untrusted provider/catalog content, plugin compromise, browser credential storage, analytics leakage, stale health, and client-only authorization.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: The chapter preserves unknown and degraded states, complete-process accessibility, server authorization, and source freshness across normal and adversarial paths.

evidence: Traced resource and operation semantics across portal, CLI, API, events, support, provider, and application verification.
Checked that browser state never becomes sole durable truth and every mutation retains principal, target, environment, request identity, authorization, and anti-forgery controls.
Checked provenance, source/observation time, stale/partial/unknown presentation, and safe degraded actions.
Checked plugin ownership, permissions, failure isolation, performance, accessibility, support, and retirement boundaries.
invariant_checking.notes: Projection, operation, authorization, accessibility, freshness, and composition invariants hold across exposition, examples, and answers.

proof_review.notes: The chapter states no theorem and contains no deductive proof.

proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No proof sketch is claimed; the operation projection is explicitly a teaching model.

evidence: The executable operation cohort is labeled synthetic and not presented as production evidence.

Normative accessibility requirements, security verification guidance, project architecture documentation, human-centered standards, service guidance, and DORA empirical/product guidance remain distinguishable.
Narrative portal examples are designs rather than measured field results, and clicks/page views are rejected as productivity or value proof.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No external accessibility conformance, penetration test, user study, or implementation audit is claimed.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter consistently treats a portal as a projection and journey channel over authoritative capability, resource, operation, evidence, authorization, and guardrail contracts. It distinguishes dashboard, catalog, shell, plugin, resource page, operation view, and source of truth.

practitioner_review.notes: A practitioner can apply the product-boundary checklist, journey/resource information architecture, full interface-state inventory, form and destructive-action patterns, complete-process accessibility plan, browser security controls, plugin manifest, deep-link and cross-channel rules, degraded-mode strategy, and privacy-aware measurement model.

pedagogical_review.notes: The sequence progresses from product boundary and information architecture through projection/state, forms, consequential actions, accessibility, security, plugins, navigation, reliability, and measurement. Ten examples remain distinct; five exercises progress from architecture to state modeling, security audit, accessibility evaluation, and safety-critical transfer, with complete answers.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
